name: Lightcast
positioning: Sells labor-market analytics, job-posting and skills data (Analyst, Labour Insight, Talent Transform, Gazelle) mainly to higher-ed, workforce boards, economic developers and employers, plus a Career Coach tool colleges give to students.
keyFeatures: Analyst platform (LMI, Alumni Pathways, Developer API)
Talent Transform / Talent Analyst for employers
pricingNote: Not public; software, consulting and API options scoped through sales, annual quotes (per G2/third-party reports).
hq: Boston, MA and Moscow, ID (offices also UK, Canada, Italy, New Zealand, India)
lastRound: Conflicting: Toolradar/Seedtable list $27M (Apr 2026); other aggregators list none; unverified
investors: KKR (Burning Glass backer; follow-on investment at 2021 merger)
ownership: Private. 2021 merger of Emsi (bought from Strada Education Network) and Burning Glass Technologies (KKR-backed); rebranded Lightcast 2022.
revenueNote: ESTIMATE from ZoomInfo/Datanyze ($167M); other aggregators range $22M (Apollo) to $105M (Prospeo) to $100-250M (LeadIQ). Not company-reported.
trafficNote: Semrush snippet for lightcast.com: ~113.8K visits in Feb (year not shown, likely 2026), down 47.7% from Jan. Similarweb shows lightcast.io global rank ~#181K (Jan 2026); visit count not readable.
weWin: Direct-to-laid-off-individual experience with coaching, reskilling and benefits help
Transparent, self-serve offering vs sales-gated enterprise contracts
theyWin: Scale and credibility of job-posting/skills data, used by hundreds of institutions
Career Coach already embedded in colleges
weNeed: Defensible, auditable LMI methodology and API
partnerIdea: License Lightcast data for skills and wage figures inside NextChapter, or position as a layoff-specific layer on top of a board's Lightcast subscription.
notes: Founded year not stated on site (Emsi ~1998, Burning Glass ~1999 per general knowledge, not verified here). Financials are aggregator estimates and conflict widely. No evidence Strada still owns it.

name: Geographic Solutions
category: Workforce case management / job bank / UI government software
positioning: Sells VOS Sapphire, a SaaS suite used by state and local workforce agencies for WIOA case management, labor exchange/job bank, LMI, fund tracking and unemployment insurance. Buyer is government, not individuals.
keyFeatures: VOS Sapphire (WIOA, Wagner-Peyser, case management, federal reporting)
GUS unemployment insurance system and REX reemployment
Virtual LMI and ALMA labor market analyzer
Virtual Career Center and job aggregation
StateRAMP/GovRAMP, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, HITRUST e1
pricingNote: Not public; SaaS fees scale with population served and modules (Business Observer).
ownership: Private, founder-led per Business Observer; no outside funding found
headcountSource: Revelio Labs ~463, Mar 2026; LeadIQ ~433 (Dec 2025); Business Observer 450 (2022)
revenueNote: Company declined to disclose; reported 20% sales growth 2020-21. Aggregator guesses range from $25-100M to $55.5M to $250-500M, too wide to use.
weWin: Consumer-grade UX and AI coaching/reskilling for the laid-off individual
Fast deployment vs multi-year state system builds
theyWin: Incumbent in state workforce systems with 1,200+ job centers
weNeed: Integration or data feed into state VOS systems
partnerIdea: Offer NextChapter coaching/reskilling and WARN data as an integrated module or referral partner within VOS-based job centers.
notes: Founded 1992 from search summary of Business Observer; website only shows copyright 1998-2026. Revenue unknown.

name: EconoVue
category: Business-engagement and economic data dashboards for workforce/economic development
positioning: Data-visualization platform giving workforce boards and economic developers business, workforce and layoff-risk data (Dun & Bradstreet, QCEW, job postings) to drive employer outreach and rapid response. Note: it is business-engagement software, not a labor-market dashboard for job seekers.
keyFeatures: Dun & Bradstreet business failure risk scores
QCEW salary time series, live job postings, CareerOneStop training data
pricingNote: Not public; free demo, free searches and trial offered.
ownership: Private, woman-owned small business; founded as The Urban Explorer, Inc. in Silicon Valley
headcountSource: Aggregators conflict: ZoomInfo 11-50, Clutch 10-49, LeadIQ ~4 (Feb 2026), Prospeo 1-10
revenueNote: ESTIMATE, ZoomInfo $6.3M; Prospeo $342K; LeadIQ range $1-10M. Very low confidence.
weWin: Serves the displaced individual directly (coaching, reskilling, benefits)
WARN data tied to individual outcomes
theyWin: Employer-side business intelligence and layoff-risk prediction (D&B data)
Existing relationships with workforce boards for Rapid Response
weNeed: Employer risk scoring / early-warning view for boards
Business-engagement CRM features for board staff
partnerIdea: Pair EconoVue's employer-risk targeting with NextChapter's worker-facing services for Rapid Response events.
notes: Brief says 'labor-market/economic dashboards'; actual focus is employer engagement. Headcount and revenue estimates conflict.

name: Hardly
category: AI career tools for workforce programs
positioning: AI career-tool platform sold to workforce development organizations, college career centers, veteran and apprenticeship programs; staff and job seekers collaborate on résumés, applications and interview practice.
keyFeatures: Claims 80% less résumé time, 10+ staff hours saved/week
pricingNote: Not public; free trial for organizations.
ownership: Private, founder-led (CEO Allison Braund-Harris, CTO Roger Harris)
weWin: Broader journey: coaching, reskilling courses, benefits and funding help
theyWin: Named customers incl. Ivy Tech, Eckerd Connects, WorkOne, Westmoreland CCC
weNeed: Staff-job seeker shared workspace with scheduling
partnerIdea: Unclear; likely a direct Program-workspace competitor, though could be resold as a résumé tool inside programs.
notes: Identified via NAWDP marketplace listing (website hardly-work.com). Single-source; no funding or size data.

name: SendCarrot
category: Participant messaging and incentives for community programs
positioning: Messaging (text, email, voice) and incentive (gift cards, Uber rides) platform for staff who track participants from intake through graduation in community colleges, workforce, adult ed, apprenticeship and reentry programs. SENDCARROT IS SHUTTING DOWN.
keyFeatures: Gift card and Uber ride incentives
weWin: Still operating, with full job-seeker services
Reskilling, coaching and data beyond messaging
theyWin: Incentive delivery (gift cards, rides) for program retention
weNeed: Participant SMS/email nudge workflows in Program workspace
partnerIdea: Its customers must migrate by Dec 15, 2026; pitch the Program workspace messaging as a replacement.
notes: Site states gift card sends end Nov 30, 2026 and messaging/accounts close Dec 15, 2026. Founding year and HQ not found.
